summary: IRAS 07251 0248 is a bright Revised Bright Galaxy Sample ULIRG with weak Chandra emission, a steep power-law fit, and evidence for heavy AGN absorption.
C3 is described as a disturbed spiral with emission along loose arms, likely interacting with a nearby spiral and belonging to the North subcluster.
The paper describes LARS03 as a complex of two merging galaxies whose ground-based data only support surface-brightness and B-K color profiles, both showing complex structure.
DEEP2-13043023 has irregular HST morphology with knots, matched emission along an arch, no velocity gradient, and mostly uniform dispersion except a high-dispersion northeast arm.
The paper classifies IRAS 09022-3615 as lower-excitation in its data but notes high-J studies require multiple excitation components, with its single-component fit giving modest density and hot gas.
The paper treats IRASF17207-0014 as a gas-rich merger with two measured black holes, a large scaling-relation offset, high star-formation requirement, and insufficient gas by its estimate.
DEEP2-13017973 was observed with the old OSIRIS grating, has spiral-like HST knots distinct from emission morphology, no velocity gradient, and high star formation rate.
The paper describes Mrk848 as a nearby major merger with tidal tails, studied through UV-to-IR photometry and MaNGA IFU spectra to compare core and tail star-formation histories.
The paper uses IRAS 23365+3604 as a moderate local ULIRG outflow template, predicting OH P-Cygni and excited-gas signatures detectable by SPICA to at least z about 1.3.
The paper revises 850.069 as a perturbed close-companion system at z=0.560, replacing catalogue morphology with a more conservative radius and Sersic index.
The paper describes 279307 as an irregular galaxy, possibly a superposition or merger, split into two COSMOS components and marginally resolved with faint point-source structure.

The paper presents Az9 as a strongly lensed z=4.274 low-mass dusty galaxy with ALMA [CII] and dust detections, a rotation-dominated disk, high obscured star formation, and unusual early dust enrichment.
The paper describes WERLS 29881 as its highest-redshift tentative LAE, with z=8.3868, inconsistent best-fit photometry partly reconciled by Ly-alpha contamination, and possible nebular excess.
Object 31 is a CANDELS galaxy selected as an LAE candidate, but its z=1.49 photometric redshift and likely O III/H emission make it a lower-redshift contaminant.
The paper defines the BCG as the brighter western cD galaxy and uses it as the center aligned with the cluster dark matter, baryons, and main mass component.
The paper identifies Source ID 330 as a local Compton-thick AGN in a barred spiral galaxy, using NuSTAR hard X-ray data to reveal heavy absorption and Fe K emission.
The paper reports no CO(1-0) or rest-frame optical emission for source 6, concludes its z=2.68 photometric redshift is unreliable, and excludes it from further analysis.
MD157 is described as a z=2.293 protocluster member, an X-ray luminous emission-line AGN, and one of the confirmed protocluster LAE counterparts.
VV 340a is an early-stage merger with a Compton-thick AGN, a large-scale dust lane, and a nuclear disk, but the OSIRIS line-ratio map shows no coherent outflow structure.
The paper classifies IC 5298 as a radio AGN, describing FRI-like 8.44 GHz morphology, a 1.49 GHz tail, outward steepening beyond 1.1, and matching mid-infrared/optical AGN evidence.
The paper reports a possible tidal connection between M86 and NGC 4402, tests removal of NGC 4402 cluster candidates, and notes nearby clusters with ambiguous host assignment.
The paper includes IRAS 14378-3651 among strong-AGN-contribution ULIRGs, notes low signal-to-noise but confirmed high terminal velocity, and computes its AGN fraction from mid-infrared diagnostics.
The paper discusses AzTEC21b as probably part of the same filamentary structure as AzTEC21a, with compatible photometric and radio/submm redshift estimates.
REBELS-38 is detected in Band 8 continuum with a two-component dust morphology, cold dust temperature, large dust mass, and low-burstiness indicators.
The paper models COLA-1's double-peaked Ly-alpha profile as potentially powered by an obscured AGN, deriving its near-zone size, ionizing emissivity, UV magnitude, and X-ray luminosity.
The paper treats HAE229 as a star-forming Spiderweb-protocluster galaxy with an extended rotating molecular gas disk and a super-galactic gas reservoir.
The thesis discusses S928 as one of two high-M/L Virgo UCDs observed in K-band CO absorption; the data show no offset from the Galactic-GC CO-metallicity relation.
Arp 256 contains one of the interacting sample’s highest-SFR hinge clumps, with an unusually luminous HST-resolved central star cluster or cluster complex.
The paper gives source 12 a CO(1-0) upper limit despite a reliable spectroscopic redshift, notes CO should have been detectable, and flags it as the main luminosity-conversion outlier.
The paper treats source 258 as an LLRG at spectroscopic redshift 0.9009 with four detected field overdensities at substantially higher redshifts.
The paper detects neutral hydrogen in ESO540-G030, measures one of the larger H I masses in the sample, and reports a significant gas-optical offset likely linked to star-forming winds.
The paper describes PGC 047197 as having only a detected central emission line, a small nuclear gas disk nearly aligned with stellar rotation, and possible internal gas loss or merger origin.
G78 is treated as a Type-1 galaxy with broad optical or NIR components and included among the paper's securely AGN-dominated sources.
The paper reports a probable CO detection for NGC4038S, estimates its molecular mass from CO(2-1), and describes it as a young, non-compact condensation in a tidal tail.
The paper reports a tentative CO(7-6) detection for COSMOS-FRI 70 at z=2.63 and argues it is a massive, star-forming elliptical BCG candidate in a distant proto-cluster.
The appendix describes Object 494057 as a rotator, noting [CII] emission, UV/optical alignment, multiple components in the ALPINE imaging and spectra.

The paper highlights EGS 29026 as one of four compact galaxies with high star-formation-rate surface density but near-zero outflow centroid velocity, considering collimated outflows and disk orientation as possible explanations.
The paper compares previous spectroscopic line detections for ESO294-G010 with new emission north of the center and gives its distances from NGC55 and NGC300.
AM 2246-490 is a LIRG in the ALMA CO/CN sample with weak but robust CN detections and the smallest CO/CN ratio in the sample.
The paper analyzes Leo I as a classical Milky Way dSph with extended recent star formation, combines 953 member-star measurements, and finds 14 candidate streams consistent with dissolving clusters.
The paper presents X-Shooter spectroscopy and a velocity-dispersion measurement for COSMOS 0050+4901, describing it as a strongly lensed, quadruply imaged, high-redshift quiescent galaxy.
